title: Console timeseries gaps and quota misreporting causing billing confusion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers and internal dashboards have reported short-duration drops ('gaps') and mismatched per-model token counts in the Console usage charts. In several cases the charts show lower consumed tokens for a model for a 1–6 hour window while backend billing/ledger records (raw events) show continuous traffic. This has caused quota/limit confusion: the Console displayed quota remaining while rate limiter had started allowing excess traffic, resulting in billing disputes. The ticket tracks investigation, root cause, mitigation, fixes, and backfill plan.
tasks: Capture and reproduce: run a controlled injection of synthetic usage events with out-of-order timestamps to reproduce gaps in the console time series (assigned to Marco)
Instrument ingestion: add ingestion-latency and event-time vs ingestion-time histograms to the metrics dashboard (assigned to Priya)
Short-term mitigation: pause auto-aggregation compaction job that dedupes later than 2h and revert the last deploy if needed (oncall)
Fix aggregator: switch aggregation to use event_time with watermarking and deterministic late-arrival merging; include event_id dedupe window (assigned to Marco/James)
Backfill job: implement idempotent backfill that re-aggregates the impacted range with strict de-duplication and append-only writes to timeseries store (assigned to SRE)
E2E tests: add a suite that replays Kafka segments with interleaved events to ensure no gaps and correct per-model attribution (assigned to Test Automation)
Customer comms: draft incident note and billing guidance for customers who saw discrepancies (assigned to PM)
Rollout: canary to 10% of traffic, monitor ingestion-latency, chart churn, and ledger discrepancy metric for 48 hours before broad rollout (assigned to Eng + SRE)
acceptance_criteria: Console time-series charts show no >=5 minute gaps for synthetic reproduction scenarios with out-of-order events
Per-model token totals from Console charts match ledger totals within 0.1% across 24h windows for three representative customers
Rate limiter and quota UI reflect consumed tokens within 60s of final event ingestion in normal load (95th percentile)
Backfill completes for the 7-day window with audit log of rows rewritten and no duplicate inflation of aggregate counts
Monitoring alerts added: ingestion_lag > 10m, aggregator_rewrite_errors > 0, discrepancy_ratio (console_vs_ledger) > 0.5%
notes: Initial symptom reported 2026-03-01 via support ticket from ACME Labs (high-volume embedding use) — they observed a four-hour dip in model:embed-1.
Preliminary hypothesis: late-arriving events were being discarded or merged incorrectly by the compaction step in the summarizer because the compact window used ingestion_time instead of event_time.
Related historical work: ENG-9821 added streaming compaction optimizations in 2025-Q4; that change assumed event_time monotonicity for local producers, which does not hold for multi-region producers.
Ledger (billing) pipeline stores raw events with event_time and event_id; we can use ledger as ground truth for discrepancy checks.
Estimated impacted customers: ~23 accounts had visible chart discrepancies in the last 30 days. Financial exposure is being assessed by Finance (request open).

runbook: If a customer reports chart gaps: 1) check ingestion_lag and aggregator backlog; 2) query ledger (raw events) for event_time distribution; 3) if late-arrival spike exists, submit backfill with idempotent job ID and monitor discrepancy_ratio.
Hotfix rollback: revert commit ingest@sha:abc123 if aggregator_rewrite_errors > 10 in first hour of canary and escalate to oncall.

Billing guidance: do not auto-credit until backfill completes and Finance signs off. Provide pro-rated credits as a customer-level remediation if aggregate billed tokens increase due to backfilled events.
